subject.title: [Feature] Pre-response enforcement hooks (hard gates) for mandatory tool-call / policy rules

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a versioned core final-delivery policy seam for fail-closed response gating, rather than treating the existing bounded revision hook or tool-only approvals as the product solution?
rationale: This establishes a new security-sensitive core/plugin API, delivery failure behavior, configuration surface, and audit contract; code review cannot safely choose those permanent product semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow response-gate RFC
options.body: Define the immutable tool ledger, terminal decision variants, fallback behavior, audit records, and cross-harness obligations before requesting implementation.

options.title: Keep enforcement tool-bound only
options.body: Document that existing tool approval and plugin hooks are the supported boundary, accepting that they do not satisfy mandatory pre-response validation.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow response-gate RFC
recommendation.body: Define the immutable tool ledger, terminal decision variants, fallback behavior, audit records, and cross-harness obligations before requesting implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest current-main seam is the typed plugin finalization-hook surface this contributor has repeatedly shaped.
